title: Run a single command as another user
summary: Execute a specific command as another user (like root) without switching your entire shell session. You will need to enter that user's password.

aliases.text: run one command as another user

steps.explain: Use `su - <username> -c "<command>"` to run a single command as the specified user. The command is passed as a string.

placeholders.name: USERNAME
placeholders.description: The user to run the command as (e.g., root).

placeholders.name: COMMAND
placeholders.description: The command you want to execute.

rollback.explain: This action does not change your shell state, so no rollback is needed. If the command modified files, you would need to undo those changes manually.

warnings: You must know the password of the user you are running the command as.
Be careful when running commands as root, as they can affect the entire system.
